chunks: And she in whose house he resided wished to seduce him and, closing the doors, said: "Come into me." He said: "God forbid! He is my master who has approved my stay. Surely those who act wrongly do not prosper."

key_terms.أَحْسَنَ مَثْوَايَ: He has approved my stay / treated me well
key_terms.الَّتِي هُوَ فِي بَيْتِهَا: The one (wife of Aziz) in whose house he resided
key_terms.عَنْ نَفْسِهِ: To seduce him / take his self
key_terms.هَيْتَ لَكَ: Come into me / Here I am for you

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Joseph say when the wife of Aziz tried to seduce him?
ai.summary: In this verse, Prophet Joseph (Yusuf) rejects the wife of Aziz's seduction by invoking 'Mazhad Allah' (fear of God) and acknowledging his master's kindness, highlighting the dual pillars of divine consciousness and gratitude in resisting temptation. Shia scholars often emphasize that his refusal was not merely out of duty to his master but rooted in a profound awareness of Allah's presence, making him a model of chastity and integrity. The concluding phrase 'indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed' serves as a universal promise of ultimate justice for those who remain steadfast in their faith despite worldly pressures.
